# MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

Scope
This document provides controlled maintenance instructions for lubrication and fluid handling on EQ-P1-L2-HT03. It covers selection, inventory, delivery, application, and recordkeeping necessary to maintain reliable operation of the heat treat quench and fluid management subsystems. It applies to maintenance personnel and technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 in plant P1, line P1-L2. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-01, SOP-P1-L2-02, and SOP-P1-L2-03 for related operating and safety procedures.

Tools
- Clean funnel and spill tray dedicated to EQ-P1-L2-HT03 fluid fills.  
- Labeled containers compatible with CFW-LUB-465.  
- Approved personal protective equipment as defined in SOP-P1-L2-02.  
- Electronic maintenance log terminal or paper log forms per SOP-P1-L2-01.  
- Visual inspection mirror and flashlight for inaccessible lubrication points.

Background and rationale
Proper lubrication and quench fluid control reduce wear, prevent unplanned downtime, and ensure consistent metallurgical results from the heat treat cycle. The quench timing is critical to metallurgical outcome; control of post-quench handling reduces distortion and surface defects. The lubricant specified for moving mechanical linkage and pump bearings is identified to ensure chemical compatibility with seals and quench fluid. Adherence to the documented maximum for quench delay is required to maintain process capability and repeatability.

Critical values
- The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds.  
- The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is CFW-LUB-465.

Procedure
Pre-activity checks
- Verify machine is in maintenance mode and locked and tagged per SOP-P1-L2-02 before any fluid handling.  
- Confirm that required PPE is in place and that spill containment is prepared.  
- Pull the maintenance history for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 from the maintenance log. Cross-reference the last lubricant change and quench system inspection against SOP-P1-L2-01.

Lubricant handling and application
- Use only lubricant with part number CFW-LUB-465 for the specified bearing points and linear guides on EQ-P1-L2-HT03. Confirm label legibility before opening containers.  
- Clean the lubrication fitting area to remove contaminants and old residue using lint-free cloths.  
- Dispense lubricant using clean dispensers dedicated to CFW-LUB-465 to avoid cross-contamination. Apply until the fitted clearance is visibly saturated and excess is wiped away. Do not add any other additives or fluids.

Quench system fluid checks and control
- Inspect the quench fluid reservoir for clarity and free-floating contaminants. If visible contamination is present, follow SOP-P1-L2-03 for fluid replacement and filtration.  
- Confirm all valve positions and pump priming per SOP-P1-L2-03 before returning the furnace to operation. Ensure that quench delivery lines are free of kinks and that the spray nozzles are seated and oriented per original equipment layout.

Quench timing confirmation
- After maintenance, perform a dry run of the sequence up to the quench event to verify mechanical actuation and timing. When initiating the quench sequence, measure the interval between furnace temperature control signal and quench engagement and ensure it does not exceed the documented maximum. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds. If measured delay exceeds this value, stop and investigate timing source, control logic, and actuation hardware. Document findings and remedial actions in the maintenance log.

Examples and failure modes
- Example: A sticky solenoid actuator allowed a delayed valve opening. Cleaning and lubrication of the actuator linkage with CFW-LUB-465 restored actuation speed and brought measured quench delay below the maximum.  
- Failure mode: Cross-contamination of lubricant with incompatible oil causes seal swelling and pump cavitation; to mitigate, use only CFW-LUB-465 containers and dedicated dispensing tools.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for EQ-P1-L2-HT03 including: technician name, tasks performed, lubricant part number used, observations of contamination, actions taken, and measured quench timing verification. Use forms and fields specified in SOP-P1-L2-01.  
- A copy of any fluid sample analyses or filter change records generated per SOP-P1-L2-03.  
- Any corrective action reports generated when quench delay exceeded the maximum, including root cause analysis and closure verification.

Acceptance criteria
- No leakage or drips present at lubrication points after completion of maintenance.  
- Only lubricant identified as CFW-LUB-465 was used; container lot identifiers and labels must be recorded in the maintenance log.  
- Quench timing validated at or below the maximum. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 24 seconds; measured values must be at or below this threshold.  
- No unresolved contamination in quench reservoir; if contamination remains, SOP-P1-L2-03 procedures must be completed prior to return to service.  
- All records filed to the controlled file cabinet and electronic maintenance system as specified in SOP-P1-L2-01.

References
- SOP-P1-L2-01  
- SOP-P1-L2-02  
- SOP-P1-L2-03

Revision and approval
- Revision control and signatures are managed electronically per SOP-P1-L2-01.
